t: At the southern end of Hanover Square stands a statue of William Pitt the Younger, Grade Two listed and put up in 1831. It was designed by Francis Leggatt Chantrey, the leading portrait sculptor of Regency Britain, who also made statues of George the Fourth and George Washington. Pitt is the man shown here: the last prime minister of Great Britain, and then the first of the United Kingdom. He held the office from 1783, again from 1804, and was still prime minister when he died in 1806.
